piece_title: Enemy AI, pursuit, variety and recovery — round 2 critique

bifurcation.note: Declared before any artifact was opened. This piece is a state machine and a parameter table; there is no art-direction or fidelity claim in it. The one image in this verdict is a bar chart of a computed metric, drawn in bare Node by my own tool, not a rendered frame. No visual reference of either era is cited anywhere.

reference_items.native_scale: M1-M9, each 0/1/2, max 18, with five hard fails independent of total
reference_items.native_score: 15/18 with the M3 chase-bot hard fail TRIGGERED
reference_items.native_verdict: The item's ladder maps 15/18 to about 6.7, but its ## Scoring section says a hard fail is independent of the total and voids the piece. checks.threshold: acquisition at 0.9R/0 deg in EVERY trial; rear never; 1.5R never; not a circle
checks.note: Measured in the browser at contention exit 0. Rear 180 never acquires and 1.5R never acquires — both PASS clauses met, and the acquisition set is not a circle, so this is not proximity aggro in a cone costume. But 0.9R at bearing 0 NEVER acquires: only the 0.5R ring does, on two of seven bearings, so the effective acquisition radius is half the declared 16 m. One of three PASS clauses fails.

checks.threshold: median SUSPICIOUS dwell >= 20 f; IDLE->AGGRO jumps <= 10%
checks.note: Median SUSPICIOUS dwell 244 f, jump fraction 0. Non-vacuous: the meter is filled by sim/stealth/system.js, not by the probe.

On the item's own fixture (stationary player, 60 s, never attacks): inf_trash 0.4373, guard_legion 0.4260, drowned_lesser 0.4358, drowned_greater 0.4221, beast_slitherfang 0.3765, champion_hist_marked 0.4320, cst_sap_speaker 0.3183. Six of seven over 0.35. Rises with duration at every start range (inf_trash at 6 m: 0.3807 / 0.4373 / 0.4399 at 1800 / 3600 / 5400 f). spacing_variance 1.09 m and state_entropy 2.31 bits both PASS, so the band logic exists — the dwell is attack recovery with 0.6-1.2 m of forward root motion, 85% of it inside 0.85*omega.

reference_items.justification: score_0_10 is 2, below 7, so no >=7 justification is owed. The 2 rather than a 0 records that eight of the nine checks pass or are marginal on measurements I took myself, that the delete-the-behaviour arm still collapses every enemy to a turning statue, and that the failing check fails on a metric whose denominator both round-1 and round-2 filed as defective. It is not a 6.7 because RI-AI01's ## Scoring section places a triggered hard fail outside the ladder.
reference_items.why_not_ten: M3's chase-bot hard fail is triggered on six of seven fighting statblocks on the fixture the item itself prescribes, and M1's 0.9R/0-degree acquisition clause never fires in the shipping game — the enemy's effective acquisition radius is half its declared sight radius.
reference_items.path_to_ten: Re-space during RECOVER rather than only after it, so the enemy is not parked inside its own strike band for 85% of its recovery frames, and re-check on the item's own fixture at three durations and four start ranges. Separately, either raise the perception fill rate or lower the declared sight radius so acquisition at 0.9R occurs within the item's 3 s hold. Then build the blind pair the item specifies and that three rounds have skipped.

checks.observed: game/src/combat/ai.js and game/src/combat/enemy.js contain zero occurrences of Math.random, disposition, faction, bounty, level, Date.now, performance.now or any weather term. Grepped directly, both files, this tree.

All six PRNG draws in ai.js (lines 496, 664, 712, 713, 714, 733, 786) go through _draw(ctx, n), which reads the simulation's single counted global core/rng.js instance. Exactly the draws RI-AI01 asks for: T05 roar length, token cooldown, T11 strafe reseed and direction, radial sign, and move selection from a range-gated eligible pool.

The behaviour_archetype table this round added maps a statblock id to a Souls-side archetype name and changes gait, leash tier, whether the body blocks and whether it backs off. It touches no hp, poise, damage, armour, frame data, moveset, reach or sight radius — the statblock still wins on both of the latter.

The one Morrowind path into the aggro latch (character/encounter.js hostile_below_disposition -> ctl.alertState = AGGRO) is untouched by this round. Round 1's ruling stands and I do not reopen it: the disposition term is binary, decides WHETHER a party opens hostile, and never modulates aggro_at_m or any frame, band, poise, speed or damage value.

status_reasons: hard_fail:RI-AI01/M3 — min_dist_dwell 0.3765-0.4373 against a chase-bot hard fail of 0.35, on six of the seven fighting statblocks, measured on the fixture RI-AI01 M3 itself specifies (stationary player, 60 s, never attacks). Robust across four start ranges and three durations, and rising with duration at every range.
2/10 min-over-axes against a 7.0 wave-1 gate. The reference-item weighted mean is 2.5 (RI-AI01 2.0 x 0.75 + RI-AI05 4.0 x 0.25) and is published so the aggregation is not a hidden choice.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM ROUND 1, and the orchestrator should not read 2 < 3 as one. The enemy's trajectory on this fixture is identical to round 1's to four decimal places (spacing_variance 1.0914 m, mean_dist 2.213 m); round 1 scored 0.1256 only because it labelled the recovery frames COMMIT and M3's denominator excludes COMMIT. Round 2 built the state that makes its own defect visible. Every axis that measures work went up: S22 5->7, consumption 4->5, closing on a fleeing player 3->7, variety 3->7.
No AR-1 failure. AR-2 not applicable — no Morrowind-side surface is touched.

The round's rejection of the round-1 verdict's own remedy (gate on closure) is UPHELD on my independent 2x2 plus a hysteresis arm the round did not build. Closure with the CIRCLE half present still never enters the strike band (2.72 m, 0 frames), and closure in any form doubles the chase-bot metric on a stationary player (0.4373 -> 0.7448). The builder was right to overrule its critic; its published proof was the weaker half of its case.

RI-AI01 M1 and M2, which the round declined to take and declined to adopt from round 1, are now measured in the browser: M1 = 1 (0.9R at bearing 0 never acquires), M2 = 2 (median SUSPICIOUS dwell 244 f). The refusal was correct in principle and vindicated in fact.

biggest_gap.what: On RI-AI01 M3's own fixture — one enemy aggroed, the player holding position and never attacking for 60 s — min_dist_dwell is 0.3183 to 0.4373 across the fighting roster against a PASS of 0.10 and a chase-bot HARD FAIL of 0.35 that six of the seven statblocks cross. The round published 0.2521 from the round-1 critic's moving fixture and scored M3 = 1/2. The cause is measured: on a passive player the enemy is in COMMIT or RECOVER for 1,896 of 3,600 frames, every attack carries 0.6-1.2 m of forward root motion, and the AI cannot steer during the swing, so it ends each attack inside its own strike band and stays there for the whole recovery (85% of recovery frames inside 0.85*omega). The number rises with duration at every start range: 0.3807 / 0.4373 / 0.4399 at 1800 / 3600 / 5400 frames from 6 m.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The player learns the rhythm of the approach before they learn the moveset, and an enemy that spends 44% of its non-swinging time inside its own reach against someone who is not even fighting back has no DANCE band from the player's chair, whatever the trace calls the states.

remedy.action: In game/src/combat/ai.js, re-space during RECOVER rather than only after it. REPOSITION already runs a sprint back-off toward circle.preferred_band_multiple; RECOVER currently only renames the leaf. The root motion is the body's and must NOT be cancelled — the commitment property (47/47 swings to full clip, zero frames in which the enemy can change its mind) is the best thing in this subsystem and must survive untouched — but the frames after hit_active ends are steerable in principle and are 85%-inside-band in practice. Declare the back-off's start frame as a leaf of game/data/combat/ai.json so the consumption census can see it. Separately, and outside this piece's files, RI-AI01 M3's denominator should be changed from 'while state != COMMIT' to 'while the enemy is in the startup or active frames of an attack', as the round-1 critic proposed in its §14.3 and this round endorsed; until that moves, the item as written is the bar.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/combat/critic-w1-12-r2-m3-chart.mjs shows min_dist_dwell <= 0.35 for EVERY fighting statblock on the item's own fixture at 1800, 3600 and 5400 frames and at start ranges 3, 6, 10 and 15 m — AND node tools/combat/w1-12-r2-teardown.mjs shows flee_frames_inside_strike no lower than round 2's base row for any statblock (inf_trash 294, guard_legion 214, drowned_lesser 320, drowned_greater 107, champion_hist_marked 752, cst_sap_speaker 13 from 12 m). The second half is not optional: M3 can be passed by making the enemy timid, and that would undo the one thing round 2 got right.

secondary_observations.what: The closure rule is structurally switched off for BEAST and SWARM. The threshold is derived rather than tuned — (walk - r) < walk_in_min_closure_mps — so it fires only when the target recedes faster than walk - 0.5. BEAST walks 2.6, needing r > 2.1, and a player walking away recedes at 2.0. Measured on the shipped tree, beast_slitherfang from 12 m reaches the strike band at player speeds 1.6, 2.2, 2.6 and 3.2 m/s and NOT at 2.0 — min gap 3.235 m, 0 frames in strike. A hole in the middle of the range sitting exactly on the speed the player spends most of the game at, and it is round 1's 'the enemy does worse against a walking player than a jogging one' surviving one archetype over. Remedy: floor the threshold at the player's own walk, or make walk_in_min_closure_mps per-archetype and say so.

Every control assertion in tools/combat/w1-12-r2-teardown.mjs (lines 232-247) tests inf_trash and nothing else, except arms A and D which are roster-wide. Arm B — the deletion of the round's entire headline — is byte-identical to base for beast_slitherfang on all four published metrics (min gap 3.235, 0 strike frames from 12 m, 81 from 4 m, dwell 0.1887), and arm E is inert for beast_slitherfang and cst_sap_speaker, while the tool prints 'all four controls moved. No arm is inert.' The round audited arm E for exactly this shape on inf_trash and did not apply the lesson across the roster it had already measured. Assert the controls per statblock.

No teardown arm deletes REPOSITION. Round 1's arm B measured that block as the one carrying M3 across its own line (0.041 -> 0.107 on the builder's fixture) and flagged it as fixture-dominated. Round 2 rebuilt the state machine around it and did not re-run the ablation.

game/data/combat/ai.json documents the design the round rejected. §movement._closure_rule and ._closure_rule_two_zones describe closure-gating and name two leaves — rush_when_closure_below_mps and chase_when_gap_opening_above_mps — as 'separate leaves', 'both 0.8 m/s'. Neither exists in the file; grep across the repo finds them only in the round-1 verdict that proposed them and in these two notes. What ships is one leaf, walk_in_min_closure_mps: 0.5, and the SAME predicate at both the APPROACH site (ai.js:612) and the CIRCLE site (ai.js:623), so the 'stricter question' the note describes for the inner zone is not asked anywhere. check-ai-units.mjs passes because it enumerates leaves that exist and cannot see two that do not. This is the file a round-3 builder reads first.

The published consumption figure is not the one in the artifacts under it. The survey and the status file say '60 of 99 leaves have a demonstrated consumer'; census.json says consumed 43 and rescue.json says rescued 11, which is 54. The survey accounts for 19 unconsumed where rescue.json's still_no_consumer lists 25; the six unaccounted are commit.tokens_by_group[0].max_size, [0].tokens, [1].max_size, [2].max_size, [2].tokens and leash.return_heal_seconds — the last a leaf round 1's census had already rescued. Perturbed on purpose-built 2-, 3- and 4-body group fixtures with two-sided perturbation, eight of the twenty-five come back consumed, so the substantive count is 62 of 99: better than claimed, by a route the round did not take.

The round's own 'real finding' about commit.swarm_max_omega_m — that it cannot be observed because the swarm branch returns swarm_tokens_at_5_plus = 3 and the row it falls through to also returns 3 — is CONFIRMED independently: the leaf is silent in swarm5, swarm6 and group5 under two-sided perturbation (x2, x0.5, 0, +1000). swarm_tokens_at_5_plus itself IS consumed (it moves at := 0 and := 9) and the round's own census.json already marks it so; the unobservable thing is the bound, not the count. Remedy: set the fallthrough row's tokens to a value that differs from the swarm branch's, or delete one of the two.

RI-AI01 M1's acquisition radius in the shipping game is half the declared sight radius. inf_trash declares 16 m; 0.9R (14.4 m) never acquires at any bearing within the item's 3 s hold, and only the 0.5R ring (8 m) does, on two of seven bearings. The alert meter reaches SUSPICIOUS at 0.9R and sits there for the whole hold. Either the fill rates in game/data/stealth/detection.json or the declared sight radius is wrong — RI-AI01 §B's '50/s at 1.0*R' should reach 100 well inside 3 s at 0.9R.

Two M1 instruments disagree about bearing 0. tools/harness/ai-browser.mjs records no acquisition at bearing 0 / 0.5R but does at 30 and 60 degrees; tools/combat/critic-w1-12-r2-m12.mjs records acquisition at bearing 0 / 0.5R at f79. Different facing conventions and different world lighting. They agree on the clause that decides the score (0.9R at bearing 0 never acquires in either), so M1 = 1 either way, but nobody should quote a per-bearing acquisition radius off either file until this is settled.

An arm I discarded rather than published, recorded so a successor does not re-derive it. My predecessor's reports/w1-12-r2-critic/closure-vs-recession.json carries an arm clFull that is byte-identical to base on six of seven statblocks across both fixtures. Its predicate computes |enemy_now - player_old| - |enemy_now - player_now|, which cancels the enemy's own motion and is therefore target recession again under another name — rule 6's second shape, an inert control. The arms in §2 of this verdict are built on a real distance window and do differ.

Closure-gating with hysteresis, which nobody has tried, DOES catch the walking player: a 30 f minimum RUSH dwell gives min gap 0.900 m and 144 frames inside the strike band, better than the shipped rule's 1.612 m. It is still the wrong answer, and the reason is not the one the round published: closure is ~0 against a player who is standing still, so it fires on RI-AI01 M3's own fixture and takes min_dist_dwell from 0.4373 to 0.7064. Recorded because the round's stated proof (oscillation) is curable and its unstated one (it fires on a stationary player) is not.

LONG_RECOVERY punish remains measured only by round 1 (7/12 against M9's own 80% bar, on the four INFANTRY statblocks). Round 2 named it and left it; I did not re-run it. The round's argument that a swinging enemy cannot punish is correct Souls behaviour and the remedy is an item-level change to what counts as a trial, not a code change.

gap_closure.measured_value: inf_trash min gap 8.14 m and 0 frames inside the strike band -> 1.612 m and 294 frames; entered_RUSH true on every statblock at every fleeing speed; 6 of 7 statblocks reach the strike band against a walking player
gap_closure.acceptance_restated: The round-1 acceptance was: for every statblock in the fighting roster and for player speeds 2.0 and 3.2 m/s, entered_RUSH true and min_gap_m <= 0.85*omega, while the 5.0 m/s row still shows the enemy losing ground; and the two new leaves must appear in the census's consumed list.
gap_closure.note: PARTIALLY closed, and the residue is specific rather than general. Reproduced independently on my own driver to three decimals. It fails the acceptance in two places: beast_slitherfang never reaches the strike band at the 2.0 m/s walk (min gap 3.235 m, 0 frames) because its archetype walk of 2.6 puts the derived threshold above the player's recession, and inf_trash does not reach it at 3.2 m/s from 12 m (4.098 m). The 5.0 m/s clause holds — 0 of 28 cells, by design. The two new leaves are in the consumed list; the two the data file's prose NAMES do not exist (see secondary observations).

corpus_extended.what: RI-AI01 M3's denominator is a property of a build's state naming rather than of the fight, and it has now decided a verdict. The identical trajectory scores 0.1256 when the recovery frames are labelled COMMIT (round 1) and 0.4373 when they are labelled RECOVER (round 2), and the chase-bot hard fail fires on one and not the other.
corpus_extended.why: Round 1's critic filed this as §14.3 and proposed the wording; round 2 endorsed it and correctly declined to fix an item that is not its file; nothing moved, and the second round in a row has now been scored against a metric both rounds agree is mis-specified. Proposed replacement for 'while state != COMMIT': 'while the enemy is in the startup or active frames of an attack'.

corpus_extended.what: RI-AI01 M3's fixture and RULES 8 are in tension and the item should say which wins. M3 says 'hold position and never attack for 60 s'; RULES 8 says a still target hides every steering defect. Here the still target is the HARSHER fixture, so nobody was hiding behind it — but two rounds have now published M3 against a moving fixture of their own invention without either declaring it as a method deviation.
corpus_extended.where: corpus/10-combat/RI-AI01-aggro-approach-spacing.md ## Comparison method, M3, against orchestration/RULES.md rule 8
corpus_extended.why: A check whose fixture two consecutive rounds silently replaced is a check that will be replaced again. The item should either bless a declared moving fixture with named amplitudes and speeds, or state that the hold-position run is normative and that any moving run is supplementary.

corpus_extended.what: RI-AI01 T01 and T03's min-dwell columns disagree with their own conditions — 60 f against '2.0 s +/-0.5' implies 30 Hz, and 90 f against '2.0 s' implies 45 Hz — while §A declares a 60 Hz fixed step in its first sentence. Both are authoring defects, and T01 has now been cited as evidence in an S22 ruling that it does not in fact support.
corpus_extended.why: S22 says a bare frame count is a defect. RI-AI01 was not in REBASE-S22-REPORT.md §Job 1 and still has not been rebased, so its ~20 bare f figures rest on an inference. The inference is right — §A declares the item's own clock before it uses a single f — but the item should say so in the table rather than leaving a builder to derive it from two rows that agree and one that does not.
